name: Fort Worth & Denver Railway
description: Fort Worth & Denver Railway, long known as the Denver Road, linked Fort Worth with the Texas Panhandle and the Colorado & Southern at Texline. Chartered in 1873, it became the Burlington system's principal Texas affiliate and retained its corporate identity until its merger into Burlington Northern on December 31, 1982.
history: The company was chartered on May 26, 1873, as the Fort Worth and Denver City Railway. Construction began from Fort Worth in 1881, the Texas and Colorado railheads met in March 1888, and through Fort Worth–Denver service began on April 1, 1888.

Following the Union Pacific, Denver and Gulf receivership, the Colorado and Southern Railway was organized in 1898 and acquired control of the FW&DC in 1899. Chicago, Burlington & Quincy acquired control of the C&S in 1908, placing the Texas road within the wider Burlington system while it remained a separate corporation.

The Texas Zephyr began operation on August 23, 1940, between Dallas–Fort Worth and Denver. FW&DC's own EMC E5A No. 9980A Silver Chief and E5B No. 9980B Silver Warrior were delivered new for the train and marked the beginning of the railroad's major diesel-passenger era.

The company was renamed Fort Worth and Denver Railway in 1951. In 1952 it consolidated the other C&S Texas properties, except Burlington-Rock Island; in 1965 it received the C&S half-interest when C&S and Rock Island absorbed that jointly owned company. FW&D remained legally separate after the 1970 Burlington Northern merger and was finally merged into Burlington Northern on December 31, 1982.

paintSchemesIntro: FW&D did not maintain a separate diesel-era paint program: its locomotives used Burlington-system schemes and, after 1970, Burlington Northern schemes. These cards document actual FW&D or FW&DC-owned and sublettered locomotives rather than duplicating generic CB&Q or BN examples.

paintSchemes.name: Texas Zephyr Passenger Silver
paintSchemes.representativeLocomotive: EMC E5A #9980A Silver Chief / E5B #9980B Silver Warrior
paintSchemes.description: FW&DC-owned E5A No. 9980A Silver Chief and E5B No. 9980B Silver Warrior were delivered new for the Texas Zephyr. Their stainless-steel appearance and red striping carried Burlington-system passenger identity rather than a uniquely FW&DC-designed scheme.

photo.alt: FW&D E5A Silver Chief, delivered as 9980A and later numbered 506, with E5B Silver Warrior in Texas Zephyr passenger paint
photo.caption: FW&DC E5A Silver Chief and E5B Silver Warrior in Texas Zephyr service; the A unit was delivered as #9980A and later carried #506.
photo.credit: Museum of the American Railroad / The Portal to Texas History · AI-assisted restoration supplied by user

paintSchemes.name: Greyback F-Unit
paintSchemes.description: FW&D received F7 sets 750–752 in August 1950. They wore the Burlington Greyback treatment with the system herald and visual identity, while their numbers and sublettering identified FW&D ownership.

photo.alt: Fort Worth and Denver EMD F7A 750A in Burlington Greyback paint
photo.caption: FW&D EMD F7A #750A in Burlington Greyback paint at Fort Worth, Texas, in 1963.
photo.credit: Castle Graphics · AI-assisted restoration supplied by user

paintSchemes.name: Blackbird / Everywhere West
paintSchemes.description: FW&D SD7 No. 855 wore Burlington Blackbird black or dark-gray and gray road-freight paint, with a Burlington Route herald, the Everywhere West side slogan, and small FW&D 855 ownership lettering. The SD7 was an FW&D locomotive in a Burlington-system scheme.

photo.alt: Fort Worth and Denver EMD SD7 855 in Burlington Blackbird Everywhere West paint
photo.caption: FW&D EMD SD7 #855 in Blackbird / Everywhere West paint at Fort Worth, Texas, in August 1972.
photo.credit: Castle Graphics · AI-assisted restoration supplied by user

paintSchemes.name: Chinese Red Switcher
paintSchemes.description: FW&D NW2 No. 605 is a documented unusual Chinese Red switcher. A 1967 Wichita Falls photograph identifies it in fresh Chinese Red paint; this individual treatment should not be read as the normal Burlington switcher scheme. The image shown here is a later 1972 Amarillo view of the same locomotive.

photo.alt: Fort Worth and Denver EMD NW2 605 in unusual Chinese Red paint
photo.caption: FW&D EMD NW2 #605 in Chinese Red paint at Amarillo, Texas, on September 30, 1972.

paintSchemes.name: BN Cascade Green / FWD
paintSchemes.description: No. 2150 was one of GP38-2s 2150–2154 associated with FW&D in 1980. It carried standard BN Cascade Green identity with FW&D/FWD ownership or sublettering while the railroad remained a separate legal corporation until 1982.

photo.alt: FW&D EMD GP38-2 2150 in Burlington Northern Cascade Green paint
photo.caption: FW&D EMD GP38-2 #2150 in BN Cascade Green paint at Pueblo, Colorado, on July 23, 1980.
